questions.question: What does a `sitemap.ts` file exporting a default function do?
options: Next.js automatically serves it at /sitemap.xml, generated from whatever entries the function returns
It only works in the Pages Router
questions.explanation: The sitemap.ts convention is picked up automatically and rendered as XML at /sitemap.xml — no manual XML writing required.

questions.question: Why would you use robots.ts to disallow a route like /dashboard?
options: To make the route load faster
To tell well-behaved crawlers not to index an authenticated-only section, while still allowing public content to be discovered
It's required for the route to function at all
To disable the route entirely for all visitors
questions.explanation: robots.ts communicates crawling rules to search engines; it doesn't block access, just discourages indexing of pages that shouldn't appear in search results.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `openGraph` field inside `generateMetadata`?
options: It supplies the title/description/image used when the page link is shared and rendered as a rich preview card on social platforms
It sets the page's primary color theme
It is only used for analytics tracking
questions.explanation: openGraph metadata is what platforms like Slack, Twitter/X, and Facebook read to render a shared link as a preview card instead of a bare URL.

questions.question: What does the `opengraph-image.tsx` file convention let you do?
options: Generate a per-page preview image on demand using JSX/CSS via next/og's ImageResponse, instead of maintaining static design assets
Only works for the root layout, not individual routes
Automatically translate images into other languages
questions.explanation: opengraph-image.tsx renders a dynamic image per route (e.g. a unique card per course) using next/og, avoiding a folder of hand-designed static previews.
